# ArgumentUnpackingCanBeUsed

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" /> <Badge type="tip" text="quick-fix" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 5.6" />

Group: [Language level migration](/rules/#language-level-migration) · PhpStorm name: `ArgumentUnpackingCanBeUsedInspection`

Since PHP 5.6, `call_user_func_array('fn', $args)` with a literal function
name can be written as a direct call with argument unpacking, `fn(...$args)`,
which is faster and easier to read and analyse.

## Example

::: code-group

```php{4,5,6,7} [Before]
<?php
class Report {
    public function build(array $cols) {
        $a = call_user_func_array('sprintf', $cols);
        $b = \call_user_func_array("max", $this->totals);
        $c = call_user_func_array('min', [3, 9]);
        $d = call_user_func_array('\\Lib\\fmt', self::defaults());

        $e = call_user_func_array([$this, 'render'], $cols);
        $f = call_user_func_array("{$this->kind}_fmt", $cols);
        $g = call_user_func_array('sprintf', $cols['main']);
        $h = call_user_func_array('sprintf');
    }
}
```

```php [After fix]
<?php
class Report {
    public function build(array $cols) {
        $a = sprintf(...$cols);
        $b = max(...$this->totals);
        $c = min(...[3, 9]);
        $d = \Lib\fmt(...self::defaults());

        $e = call_user_func_array([$this, 'render'], $cols);
        $f = call_user_func_array("{$this->kind}_fmt", $cols);
        $g = call_user_func_array('sprintf', $cols['main']);
        $h = call_user_func_array('sprintf');
    }
}
```

:::

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 4: Call &#39;sprintf(...$cols)&#39; directly using argument unpacking (wrap with array_values() when keys are not sequential).</li>
<li>line 5: Call &#39;max(...$this-&gt;totals)&#39; directly using argument unpacking (wrap with array_values() when keys are not sequential).</li>
<li>line 6: Call &#39;min(...[3, 9])&#39; directly using argument unpacking (wrap with array_values() when keys are not sequential).</li>
<li>line 7: Call &#39;\Lib\fmt(...self::defaults())&#39; directly using argument unpacking (wrap with array_values() when keys are not sequential).</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ArgumentUnpackingCanBeUsed": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore ArgumentUnpackingCanBeUsed

/**
 * @noinspection ArgumentUnpackingCanBeUsedInspection
 */
```
